description: Implement the Tauri v2 PC desktop client with React/TypeScript frontend. Connects to relay via WebSocket, supports manual dial, clipboard detection, multi-phone management, and system tray integration.
steps: Create /projects/sandbox/yunkiro/pc/ directory. Initialize Tauri v2 project with React + TypeScript template using: npm create tauri-app@latest with React-TS template, or manually scaffold the structure

Set up the frontend project structure: pc/src/ for React code, pc/src-tauri/ for Rust backend. Configure package.json with dependencies: react, react-dom, @tauri-apps/api, @tauri-apps/plugin-websocket
Create pc/src-tauri/Cargo.toml with tauri 2.x dependencies, tauri-plugin-websocket, tauri-plugin-autostart, tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager, tauri-plugin-notification

Create pc/src-tauri/src/main.rs: Tauri app setup with plugins (autostart, clipboard, notification, websocket). Register Tauri commands for: connect_relay, disconnect_relay, send_dial, send_hangup, send_sms, get_connection_status, get_phones_list

Create pc/src-tauri/src/relay.rs: WebSocket connection manager. Connects to relay URL, sends auth_request with PIN and role=pc, handles auth_response. Maintains connection state machine (DISCONNECTED/CONNECTING/CONNECTED/RECONNECTING). Auto-reconnect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s). Heartbeat ping every 30s.

Create pc/src-tauri/src/phone_manager.rs: Tracks connected phones (max 5). Stores device_id, device_name, online status, last_seen. Handles phone_hello (add phone), phone_left (mark offline). Emits events to frontend on state changes.
Create pc/src/App.tsx: Main app layout with connection status bar at top, phone list sidebar, and main dial panel
Create pc/src/components/ConnectionStatus.tsx: Shows current connection state (connected/reconnecting/disconnected), relay address, active phone count
Create pc/src/components/PhoneList.tsx: List of connected phones with name, status indicator (green=online, gray=offline), click to select active phone
Create pc/src/components/DialPad.tsx: Phone number input field + numeric keypad (0-9, *, #). Dial button, Hangup button. Input validation for Chinese mobile numbers (11 digits starting with 1)
Create pc/src/components/SMSPanel.tsx: Recipient number field, message content textarea, send button. Simple SMS template selector (dropdown with preset messages)
Create pc/src/components/PinDialog.tsx: Modal dialog for entering 4-digit PIN code on first launch. Save PIN to local storage
Create pc/src/components/Settings.tsx: Settings panel with relay URL input, PIN management, theme toggle (light/dark), autostart toggle, always-on-top toggle

Create pc/src/hooks/useRelay.ts: React hook wrapping Tauri commands. Provides: connectionStatus, phones, sendDial(number, deviceId), sendHangup(deviceId), sendSMS(number, content, deviceId). Listens to Tauri events for state updates.

Create pc/src/hooks/useClipboard.ts: Hook that monitors clipboard for phone numbers. Uses tauri clipboard plugin to read clipboard periodically (every 2s). If a valid phone number is detected, show notification/badge on dial pad.
Create pc/src/styles/: Tailwind CSS or simple CSS with light/dark theme variables. Compact layout targeting ~400x600px window.
Configure pc/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json: window settings (title, size 400x600, resizable, decorations), system tray configuration, autostart capability, app identifier
Write frontend tests: pc/src/__tests__/DialPad.test.tsx (number validation, dial button state), pc/src/__tests__/PhoneList.test.tsx (render phones, select active)
Verify: npm install succeeds, npm run build (frontend) compiles, cargo build (src-tauri) compiles
acceptance_criteria: npm install in pc/ completes without errors
Frontend builds successfully (npm run build or equivalent)
Tauri Rust backend compiles (cargo build in src-tauri/)
Frontend renders: PIN dialog, connection status, phone list, dial pad
WebSocket connection logic in Rust handles auth handshake with relay
Phone state updates (phone_hello/phone_left) propagate to frontend
Dial command sends properly formatted JSON message through WebSocket
findings: Frontend builds and tests pass. Rust backend type-checks (cargo check) successfully. Full cargo build requires webkit2gtk-4.1 and javascriptcoregtk-4.1 system libraries which are not available on Amazon Linux 2023. This is expected - the app targets Windows/Ubuntu/macOS desktop environments. Used fake pkg-config files to verify cargo check passes. 11 frontend tests pass (DialPad validation, PhoneList rendering). The tray-icon feature is included in tauri deps. tokio-tungstenite v0.24 used for WebSocket. Protocol message format matches relay server exactly.
